sections.h2: Which sale path suits a Kettering house best?
sections.html:
A Kettering owner who wants top dollar and has time should list with an agent, while an owner facing a deadline, heavy repairs or an estate usually gets further with a cash buyer. Selling alone sits in between, since the commission stays with you along with every task.

  • Listing: the broadest exposure, with the schedule set by buyer financing and the appraisal.
  • Owner sale: lower cost and more legwork, and the buyer is still owed the state property disclosure form.
  • Cash purchase: a quick close on the house as it is, which matters when the roof, furnace or wiring would scare off a lender.

Ownership runs high in Kettering: 64.9 percent of households hold title to the home they live in, and 86.5 percent of residents stayed put over the previous year. Sales here tend to involve long held houses with years of accumulated repairs and records.

Kettering had 57,396 residents in mid 2025, a dip of less than one percent from 2020. The city filled in during the 1950s and 1960s and has plenty of postwar houses, so buyers often ask about wiring, plumbing and windows.

With nearly one in five residents 65 or older, expect long held houses and estate sales to make up a fair share of what comes to market.

Kettering is served by the Kettering City School District, which includes Kettering Fairmont High School. Use the district name accurately in a listing and point buyers to the district office for attendance questions, since city and district boundaries can differ.

The city counts 20 parks, the Fraze Pavilion concert venue, Rosewood Arts Center and Pondview Park's nature trails. The Greater Dayton Regional Transit Authority runs buses, and the typical worker spends about 20.3 minutes getting to work. Dayton, Oakwood and Riverside lie to the north, Moraine and West Carrollton to the west, and Centerville and Beavercreek to the south and east.

Kettering reviews construction through its Planning and Development Department, reachable at 937-296-2441. Under Ordinance 1301, a project needs approval from every city department that applies, whether building, fire, zoning or stormwater, before work starts. The city aims to finish reviews in 10 days and says it can take up to 30 when demand is high.

  • Certificate of Occupancy: issued only after the required inspections pass and every department signs off.
  • Finished work: if you added a deck, finished a basement or replaced a furnace, locate the permit and final inspection record before you list.
  • Rental condition: the city's landlord and tenant guide requires an owner to keep mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems up to code, heating able to hold 68 degrees, and water heating at no less than 110 degrees at the taps.

A structure that fails the code can be condemned and posted as unfit for human habitation, so cure visible violations early. A rental seller can also point the buyer to the same guide to show what was maintained.

sections.h2: How is a deed transferred in Montgomery County?
sections.html:
Because Kettering sits in Montgomery County, the County Auditor processes the deed transfer, and this step is needed for the transfer to count as a legal transaction. The conveyance fee is $3 per $1,000 of the actual sale price plus $.50 for each parcel. Call 937-225-4373 with questions. Filers can also use ePN or Simplifile for electronic submission.

Ohio Revised Code 319.202 requires the buyer's side to file a statement declaring the property's value, and it puts the fee on the seller. A seller who has claimed a property tax reduction should expect to answer a question about it on that statement.

sections.h2: Ohio's disclosure form for Kettering sellers
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 covers the disclosure form for one to four unit homes. It lists exceptions such as transfers by court order, by an executor or other fiduciary, and between spouses or parents and children. Most arm's length sales of a Kettering house do need the form.

Selling as is does not change that. A house with an old furnace or dated wiring can sell, but you still answer the form honestly about problems you know of. Cash buyers price the repair in, while financed buyers may ask you to fix it.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer the right call for a Kettering owner?
sections.html:
Take a cash offer when the sale must follow your timetable and the house would struggle in a conventional listing. Examples include a worn mid century home, a property with a code citation still open, or an estate whose heirs live elsewhere.

Get every offer in writing and weigh it against what an agent would likely net after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Settle who pays title and recording fees plus the Montgomery County transfer charge, and keep your own copy of the disclosure form and any permit records for the buyer.

Ask what the buyer does if a walkthrough finds something new, and get the closing date in writing. A firm date matters most when you are paying for a second household or carrying an empty house.

Some homework up front prevents problems at the closing table.

  1. Pull permit records for any deck, basement finish or furnace replacement, and ask the Planning and Development Department whether the final inspection passed.
  2. Walk the house for visible code problems and fix them, because a failed structure can be condemned.
  3. If you rent the house, gather the lease and the maintenance records that show heat, water heating and wiring were kept up.
  4. Fill out the disclosure form and keep a signed copy.
  5. Ask the title company to confirm the Montgomery County charge so it shows on the settlement statement.

A cash sale compresses this list into a few days, but the permit records and the disclosure form are still yours to supply, and any serious buyer will ask for them. If heirs live elsewhere, one person with authority to sign should collect the papers and be the contact for the title company. Keeping everything in one folder, paper or digital, makes it easy to hand the buyer a complete record on request.

faqs.q: What is the Montgomery County transfer charge on a Kettering sale?
faqs.a: The conveyance fee is $3 per $1,000 of the actual sale price plus $.50 per parcel. Under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 the seller bears that charge, and it should show on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Will a buyer ask for permit records on a Kettering house?
faqs.a: Buyers and lenders sometimes ask for one. Kettering's Planning and Development Department at 937-296-2441 can tell you what was permitted and whether a final inspection was passed.

faqs.q: Can a Kettering house sell with an outdated furnace or wiring?
faqs.a: Yes, a house can sell as is, but the seller still completes the Ohio disclosure form under Revised Code 5302.30 and answers honestly about known problems. Cash buyers price the repair in, while financed buyers may ask the seller to fix it.

faqs.q: Which school district do Kettering addresses belong to?
faqs.a: Most addresses are in the Kettering City School District, whose high school is Kettering Fairmont. City and district boundaries can differ, so a buyer should verify a particular address with the district office.

faqs.q: Who handles property maintenance complaints about a Kettering rental?
faqs.a: The city's Planning and Development Department answers questions about the code at 937-296-2441. The landlord guide on the city site lists the standards for walls, hallways, plumbing, heating and wiring that owners must meet.
